items.zh: 黄仁勋复职原因
items.en: Reasons for Jensen Huang's return to duty
items.note: Nvidia announced that its board of directors has unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as its president, chief executive officer, and a board member. The company stated that this decision followed discussions with Huang and consultations with high-level U.S. government officials, who confirmed that his return poses no national security risk. Nvidia's chairman and the former acting CEO remain in their respective roles as the company continues to cooperate with ongoing government inquiries.

items.zh: 金价
items.en: Gold prices
items.note: International gold prices have fallen below $3,600 per ounce, marking a 14-month low due to a combination of rising US interest rate expectations and liquidity pressures in the stock market. An economist explains that while short-term factors like algorithmic trading have amplified the drop, long-term support remains from central banks buying gold for reserves. Major financial institutions have adjusted their future price forecasts downward but still anticipate a recovery once monetary policy shifts. The article presents this as a temporary correction rather than the end of the gold market's long-term bullish trend.

sources.name: China News Service
sources.title: 黄金跌跌不休，何时反弹？
sources.titleEn: Gold prices continue to fall, when will they rebound?

items.more: Zhaolian's chief economist Dong Ximin identifies the key drivers as re-pricing of US monetary policy and a liquidity squeeze from tech stock adjustments. Goldman Sachs lowered its 2027 gold price target to $4,650 per ounce, while UBS adjusted its 2026 target to $4,500 per ounce. Despite these cuts, Goldman predicts gold could reach $5,600 by 2028 if the Federal Reserve begins cutting rates. Dong suggests that gold prices will likely oscillate widely through 2026 before facing less pressure in 2027.

items.zh: “月租”酒店划不划算
items.en: Is renting a hotel room by the month cost-effective?
items.note: Renting hotel rooms by the month is emerging as a cost-effective alternative to traditional housing in cities like Shanghai, with some guests saving nearly 2,000 yuan monthly compared to renting small apartments. Major hotel groups are entering this long-term rental market by offering services that include breakfast and cleaning, targeting short-term transitions rather than permanent living. Experts distinguish between 'settling down' rentals, which resemble standard leases, and 'travel-style' rentals that offer flexibility but lack the legal protections of residential housing contracts.

sources.name: China News Service
sources.title: “月租”酒店划不划算？先分清“安居”与“旅居”
sources.titleEn: Is a 'monthly rent' hotel worth it? First, distinguish between 'settling down' and 'traveling'

items.more: The article notes that the domestic mid-to-long stay market has a gross merchandise value of approximately 240 billion yuan, which is small compared to the 3 trillion yuan housing rental market. Industry figures suggest hotels will focus on the mid-to-high-end white-collar and transitional housing segments, using their service quality to justify premiums. While some guests complain about noise and hygiene, hotel representatives argue that their business model avoids the deposit disputes common in traditional rentals.

items.more: Jensen Huang, a co-founder who has led the company for over 30 years, stepped down on November 12 after reports of extramarital affairs emerged. Although he has been reappointed, he must still attend a closed-door inquiry by a U.S. House committee to explain whether the company complied with export control regulations. U.S. President Trump commented that he had communicated with the board and agreed that reinstating Huang was the correct decision. The article notes that Huang expressed gratitude for the support he received and looks forward to returning to work.

items.zh: 教育部就教材管理条例征求意见
items.en: The Ministry of Education seeks public opinion on textbook management regulations.
items.note: China's Ministry of Education has launched a public consultation on a draft regulation governing textbook management. The ministry states that this initiative aims to strengthen the legal framework for educational materials, ensuring high quality and alignment with national goals. The proposed rules cover the entire lifecycle of textbook development, from planning to distribution, and emphasize the role of Party leadership in the process. This move seeks to codify successful practices into formal regulations to support the long-term development of China's educational system.

items.more: The draft regulation consists of eight chapters and 67 articles, detailing specific requirements for quality control and management mechanisms. The Ministry of Education conducted extensive research, consulting with legal and education experts, as well as various government bodies and schools across the country. These efforts were designed to ensure the rules are practical, forward-looking, and effective. The article does not specify a deadline for the public comments or the expected timeline for the regulation's final adoption.
